sub_answers.sub_question: Enumerate all formal criminal or administrative investigations, indictments, or prosecutions initiated against the politician (include investigating agency names, case/file numbers, start dates, criminal or statutory charges alleged, and final dispositions or current statuses).
sub_answers.text: Four criminal indictments were filed against Donald Trump in 2023: two state indictments (New York and Georgia) and two federal indictments (one in Florida and one in the District of Columbia) [d73425097s0p0]. In Georgia, Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis convened a grand jury and a 23‑member grand jury returned indictments on August 14, 2023, charging Trump and 18 co‑defendants under Georgia's RICO statute and related counts for efforts to overturn the 2020 election; the indictment initially contained 13 charges against Trump (later reflected as eight remaining counts after dismissals) [d74593923s0p0] [d73425097s4p0]. The Georgia prosecution was paused, Willis was disqualified from prosecuting in December 2024, the Georgia Supreme Court declined to hear her appeal in September 2025, Pete Skandalakis announced he would take on prosecution duties in November 2025, and Skandalakis dropped all charges against all remaining defendants on November 26, 2025, ending the case [d73425097s4p0] [d74593923s0p0]. Supreme Court ruling on presidential immunity for official acts and subsequent prosecutorial and personnel developments in the Justice Department; DOJ policy changes and the resignation of special counsel Smith were factors cited in the dismissals [d73425097s0p0]. Donald Trump pleaded not guilty to all charges initially and was convicted in the New York case while the Georgia and the two federal cases were ultimately dropped or dismissed as described above [d73425097s0p0].

He led the FDP's delegation in the 2021 coalition negotiations' working group on financial regulation and the national budget (co-chaired with SPD and Green counterparts), during the post-2021-election traffic light coalition talks [d21081409s3p0]. He was elected leader of the FDP parliamentary group in December 2021 and re-elected by 93 percent of his parliamentary group's members in 2023, positions that structured his parliamentary leadership authority and strategy [d21081409s3p0]. He held committee assignments in the Bundestag's Foreign Affairs and Digital Affairs committees, acted as his parliamentary group's coordinator in the Digital Affairs committee, was vice-chair of the German Parliamentary Friendship Group for Relations with the Maghreb States, and was a member of the NATO Parliamentary Assembly and the Parliamentary Assembly of the Union for the Mediterranean, using those committee and delegation roles as formal parliamentary instruments [d69377803s2p0][d69377803s2p0].
